subject: Human Body
title: Protecting the Brain
description: A 60-second lesson on Protecting the Brain.

hook.text: The brain is soft as tofu. It needs layers of protection. The skull is just the outermost shield.

buildup.text: Three membranes called meninges wrap the brain. Between them, cerebrospinal fluid cushions every impact.

discovery.text: Cerebrospinal fluid lets the brain float, reducing its effective weight from 1.4 kg to about 25 grams.

twist.text: A hard hit can still slam the brain against the skull's inner wall. That's how concussions happen.

climax.text: Repeated concussions cause lasting damage. The skull can't protect against forces from within.

punchline.text: Bone, membranes, fluid. Three layers for one irreplaceable organ.

quiz.question: How much does the brain effectively weigh when floating in cerebrospinal fluid?
